title: Dialog
summary: A dependency-free modal with native focus handling, keyboard dismissal, and a small CSS token surface.
overview: A progressively enhanced modal built on the native dialog element. The live example runs the exact stored HTML, CSS, and JavaScript in an isolated browser session.

component.useWhen: Use a modal when a focused decision or short task must be completed before returning to the current page.
component.avoidWhen: Avoid it for passive information, long forms, multi-step flows, or content that deserves its own page.

examples.title: Confirmation dialog
examples.description: Open the modal, dismiss it with Escape or the backdrop, and verify that focus returns to the trigger.

anatomy.name: Trigger
anatomy.description: A native button that opens the modal and receives focus again after dismissal.

anatomy.name: Dialog
anatomy.description: The native top-layer container responsible for modal focus behavior and Escape handling.

anatomy.name: Header
anatomy.description: An optional eyebrow and required heading that provide the accessible name.

anatomy.name: Body
anatomy.description: Concise context describing the decision and its consequences.

anatomy.name: Actions
anatomy.description: A method=dialog form that closes without custom button handlers.

tokens.name: --dialog-accent-text
tokens.description: Text shown on the primary action.

tokens.name: --dialog-radius
tokens.description: Corner radius of the dialog surface.

tokens.name: --dialog-shadow
tokens.description: Elevation applied to the modal surface.

accessibility: The native dialog element supplies modal semantics, focus containment, and Escape dismissal.
aria-labelledby and aria-describedby connect the heading and explanation to the dialog.
Focus returns to the opening control after every close path.
The visible focus ring remains available for keyboard users.
component.responsive: The dialog width is capped on larger screens. Below 32rem, actions stack vertically with the safest action last in visual order and first in DOM order.
limitations: Use only one modal interaction at a time; nested dialogs create confusing focus and dismissal behavior.
The confirmation event reports intent but does not perform application-specific work.
Very old browsers without native dialog support require a polyfill, which is intentionally not included.

provenance.label: Original native implementation
provenance.note: Built from platform primitives for Dev Lib; no third-party component source is included.
